text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Voters cut Liberals down to size: Reform to be Official Opposition; New Democrats, Tories regain status in House.
- Reform becomes opposition: Party builds on B.C., Alberta base but fails to make inroads in Ontario.
- Liberal unity agenda part of election debris: Despite keeping his majority, Chretien emerges a wounded leader.
- Growls of resentment loud on both sides of Rockies: Deep-seated bitterness found a voice in Manning campaign.
- McVeigh guilty in Oklahoma bombing: Former soldier now faces sentencing phase of trial, which could lead to execution.
- Economy steams ahead: GDP grows 0.8 percent in quarter on exports and spending, but taxes shrink personal income.
- Ault rejects Saputo offer as inadequate: C$28-a-share bid panned as profit forecast to jump 32.5 percent.
- Amber reveals huge Alberta oil reserves: Projection soars to 114 million barrels.
- UGG deal part of ADM's global push: Giant looks to diversify outside U.S.
- Big shakeup for regulators: New era is near for securities watchdogs, as Alberta and British Columbia harmonize procedures and Ontario and Quebec look set to get free rein from their governments.
